high.title: Oil Prices Plummet Over 11% as Iran Announces Good News from Strait of Hormuz
high.summary: Global oil prices fell sharply on Friday 17/4 after Iran sent positive signals about maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz - the world's most critical energy transportation route. Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi announced that the Strait of Hormuz is now "completely open" during the ceasefire implementation, easing concerns about oil supply disruptions. WTI crude for May delivery dropped over 11% to around $84/barrel, while Brent crude for June fell over 10% to around $89/barrel. This represents a significant cooling in energy markets, with US crude losing the $90/barrel threshold. For Vietnamese markets, this oil price decline could ease inflationary pressures and potentially reduce import costs, benefiting the trade balance. However, investors should monitor geopolitical developments closely as the situation remains volatile and could impact global risk sentiment and capital flows to emerging markets like Vietnam.

high.title: Iran Announces Complete Opening of Strait of Hormuz
high.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister announced that commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is declared "completely open" during the ceasefire period, though vessels must follow a "coordinated route" published by Iranian maritime authorities. President Trump thanked Iran but stated that US naval blockade of Iranian ports remains in effect until a deal is reached. Oil prices dropped over 10% below $90/barrel. This development is crucial for global energy markets and could impact Vietnam's trade balance and inflation outlook.

high.title: Oil Tankers Only Allowed in 'Drops': Iran Declares Absolute Control of Hormuz
high.summary: The Strait of Hormuz situation reversed dramatically as Iran announced renewed tight control just hours after the US claimed full reopening. Iran's Revolutionary Guard stated the strait remains under "strict management by armed forces" and will not open completely while the US maintains naval blockade of Iranian ports. This flip-flop has caused oil tankers to turn around mid-journey in the Persian Gulf and pushed energy markets back into uncertainty. The White House maintains Hormuz is "completely open for commercial traffic." This volatility directly impacts global energy pricing and could affect Vietnam's import costs, inflation expectations, and currency stability through oil price fluctuations.

medium.title: MB Bank Just Adjusted Interest Rates: Which Term Has the Highest Rate?
medium.summary: MB Bank reduced deposit rates across multiple terms, with 6-11 month rates down 0.1% to around 4.6%/year and 12-18 month terms down 0.2% to 6.3%/year. The 24-month term dropped 0.3% but remains highest at 7.2%/year, while long-term 36-60 month rates fell 0.5% to 7.0%/year.

medium.title: Q1 2026 Results Update for MB, VPBank, ACB: One Bank Posts Pre-tax Profit of VND 9,500 Billion
medium.summary: MB Bank reported strong Q1 results with pre-tax profit reaching VND 9,500 billion (up 13.3% YoY), credit growth of 3.3% to VND 1.146 trillion, and deposit growth of 0.73%. ACB posted VND 5,400 billion pre-tax profit (up 17% YoY), while other major banks also showed positive momentum in the first quarter.

medium.title: Over VND 11 Million Billion in Real Estate Collateral at Vietcombank, VietinBank, BIDV, Agribank and MB
medium.summary: Total collateral assets at Vietnam's Big 5 banks reached nearly VND 16 trillion by end-2025, up 20.4% YoY. Real estate collateral dominated at over VND 11.6 trillion (up 22.1%), representing 73% of total collateral portfolio, indicating continued heavy reliance on property-backed lending across the banking system.

medium.title: Proposal to Continue Reducing Gasoline Import Taxes to 0% Until June 30
medium.summary: Ministry of Finance proposes extending zero import tariffs on gasoline and oil products by two months to June 30, 2026. The current Decree 72 reduced MFN tariffs from 10% to 0% for gasoline and 7% to 0% for diesel/jet fuel, aimed at controlling domestic fuel price pressures.

medium.title: World's Largest Gold Fund Accumulates Dozens of Tons of Gold for 4 Consecutive Days
medium.summary: SPDR Gold Trust bought over 7.7 tons of gold on April 17, bringing total holdings above 1,060 tons after four consecutive days of net purchases totaling 13.4 tons. Gold prices recovered to around $4,800/oz, up 1.7% for the week and 9% since late March.
